newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA NAMES ADVISERS TO SUN AIR PRIVATISATION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA NAMES ADVISERS TO SUN AIR PRIVATISATION.

text.p: The South African government announced on Friday that investment bank BOE NatWest and law firm Moseneke and Partners had been appointed jointly to advise it on the privatisation of domestic airline Sun Air.
The partnership of BOE Natwest and Moseneke was selected from a short-list of three bidders.
They were recommended by an evaluation committee made up of government, its overall privatisation advisers Hong Kong Shanghai Banking Corp, labour and Sun Air management.
Sun Air is one of seven public sector corporations Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau has said will be at least partly privatised by the end of 1997.
Sigcau said late last month that Sun Air, tourist resort group Aventura, mining group Alexcor and transport group Autonet would be fully privatised.
Strategic equity stakes are to be sold in telecommunications utility Telkom, the Airports Company which runs South Africa's major airports and forestry group Safcol.
South African Airways, the national carrier, is to seek a foreign equity partner by the middle of next year.
Virgin Atlantic Airways has already expressed an interest in buying the airline to develop it into a pan-African low-cost regional carrier.

At the launch of Virgin's service between London and Johannesburg last October, owner Richard Branson said the local airline would form the base for developing a pan-African network on the model of Branson's Virgin Express shorthaul airline in Europe.
"It depends on what the price is but yes, we would like to look at it," Branson said.
Tom Boardman, managing director of BOE Natwest said the appointment of an adviser sent a strong signal from government of their commitment to the privatisation process.
"I think the fact that Sun Air is a small transaction is not of crucial importance. It is the fact that it is being done that is the important aspect," he said.
Government has been criticised for its lack of progress in privatising state-owned assets, a key component of its macro-economic package unveiled in June last year.
Boardman said that in seeking to get the best possible price for the airline, the advisers would seek parties both locally and internationally for prospective buyers of the airline.
He said that while he could give no indication of when the tendering process would begin, the advisory group had been briefed to expedite the process of privatisating the airline.
The advisory group would meet the restructuring committee this weekend, he added.

"The process will include full consideration for all the stakeholders in the business and previously disadvantaged groups in South Africa and the best long-term stakeholder which may be a minority or majority share," Boardman said.
Telkom is expected to announce the selection of a strategic equity partner by March this year.
Boardman could not comment on how long the process of privatising Sun Air was expected to take.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
